title.narrative: Tanzania. Empowering. Citizens and Safeguarding Rights for Inclusive, Transparent and Accountable Public Spending
Tanzania. Empowering. Citizens and Safeguarding Rights for Inclusive, Transparent and Accountable Public Spending

description.narrative:
This proposed project seeks to strengthen democratic governance and human rights in Tanzania by promoting citizen engagement in public finance processes and enhancing accountability in the use of public resources. Recognising that democratic participation and human rights are inextricably linked with transparent and inclusive governance, the project will enable citizens—particularly women, youth and people living with disability (marginalised groups)—to engage meaningfully in policy discussions, budget processes, and social accountability initiatives. It will also strengthen civil society capacities to monitor, report on, and respond to governance and human rights developments in the country.
The project will focus on bridging the gap between citizens and decision-makers through evidence-based advocacy, public education campaigns, and local-level dialogues. Special emphasis will be placed on making public finance issues more accessible to ordinary citizens, especially women, youth, People with Disabilities (PWD) and rural communities, and enabling them to hold duty bearers accountable for the equitable allocation and effective use of public resources. The proposed project intends to achieve Enhanced democratic governance and equitable development through transparent, inclusive, and accountable use of public resources in Tanzania.
It will deliver the following key outcomes: Outcome 1: Empowered citizens monitor democratic processes for inclusive governance. Outcome 2: Increased Citizen engagement for inclusive decision-making that enhances equitable and accountable use of public resources.
Citizens will be the primary beneficiaries of the proposed project. Other actors include Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), Media and Religious Leaders. Website: https://www.policyforum-tz.org/
